fields.description: The opaque docname series. Nothing about the volunteer, the date or the place goes in the primary key.
fields.label: Series

fields.description: Whose time this is. Identity is read through the volunteer's Red Profile, never copied onto this record.
fields.label: Volunteer

fields.description: Which structural kind of log this is, and the only field on this record that changes what the server will accept. general: volunteering that stands on its own (training, an open day, office support), and which may never name a deployment. deployment: time served on a specific deployment, and constrained to deployments this volunteer actually took part in. This is a closed, code-owned set rather than a society's vocabulary, because each value names a different validation rule and a society adding a third value would produce a log nothing knows how to check. The society's own vocabulary is log_category next to it. Nothing branches on this value with a scattered comparison: volunteer/services/timelog.py holds one dispatch table keyed by it, exactly as the member module's approval_mode does. See deployment for the ownership rule the second kind carries.
fields.label: Log Type

fields.description: How the society classifies this time for its own reporting: training, community event, office support. A configurable vocabulary a society extends freely, and deliberately separate from log_type: no code anywhere branches on a category value. Optional, because a society that does not categorise its volunteering should not be forced to.
fields.label: Category

fields.description: ACC-02. Where this time was served. Required on every log of every type, because every log happened somewhere: an unplaced log is invisible to geo scoping and cannot be reported on by the branch whose work it was. Enforced by the controller before the log_type dispatch runs, so it holds for a kind of log that has not been built yet as much as for one that has.
fields.label: Geo Node

fields.description: The day the time was served. A log is filed against a date rather than a range, so a week of volunteering is a week of logs and each one can be placed and categorised separately.
fields.label: Activity Date

fields.description: How many hours were served. Must be greater than zero, since a log of no time is not a record of anything, and no more than the hours in a day, since a log claiming more than that is a typo rather than a very long shift.
fields.label: Hours

fields.description: Which deployment this time was served on. Two rules hold and both are enforced on the server by the controller, on every path a log can arrive by. A general log carrying a value here is rejected outright, because general volunteering is by definition not deployment time. A deployment log is rejected unless the deployment named here lists this volunteer on its participants. That second rule is ownership, not geo: being correctly placed in the right county does not make somebody a participant, so the picker filter is a convenience and the server check is the control. Fabricating participation by typing a deployment's name is therefore impossible rather than merely hidden.
fields.label: Deployment

fields.description: What the volunteer actually did, in whoever is filing the log's own words.
fields.label: Notes
